narratives.Description: fix(hooks,security): fail closed on unknown writes to UAT-protected destinations
narratives.Overview:
## What to build

Implement one destination-anchored UAT decision for Shell commands that target protected Directive paths. If a command is write-shaped and the classifier cannot prove that it is read-only, it must emit a protected-operation decision and fail closed instead of falling through as `shell-op-unclassifiable`.

Turn the writer families reported in #3593, #3626, #3728, #3764, #3804, #3849, #3918, #3953, and #4161 into a table-driven regression corpus within the same delivery slice. The binary names are test inputs, not separate recognition branches.

Protected destinations include `.deft/authz/**`, `.deft/approved-scope/**`, `.deft-directive-disable`, and `.no-deft-directive`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unknown write-shaped Shell forms targeting each protected-destination class fail closed while UAT is active.
- [ ] Commands proven to be read-only are not blocked solely because they mention a protected path.
- [ ] Regression tests cover every writer family in the nine source AppSec reports.
- [ ] Tests cover authz-grant forgery, kill-switch planting, and approved-scope minting.
- [ ] The decision code and copy distinguish this case from an ordinary unclassified allow.
- [ ] Relevant security and hook tests pass.
- [ ] `task check` passes.

## Type

AFK

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.

### Comment by @dbcall2 (2026-09-12T21:06:58Z)

model: claude-opus-5
role: critic

Charter: refutation. Round 1, fresh critic, ceiling 5648649724 (in-ceiling input: issue body + triage write-back 5648649724). Body digest verified `sha256:b3c228ea59c19e7fbbce959dfe7a6d3d1382435ce9ffa4c60964f95046d04026`. All probes run at dispatch SHA `4011eb1`, read-only; `git status --porcelain` clean after each.

## Re-verification (ran the checks; cites below are outputs, not line claims)

Probe: `classifyShellAuthzOps` on one representative command per source report, executed at `4011eb1`.

```
FAIL-OPEN          #3849 typst compile doc.typ .deft-directive-disable
gated[settings]    #3849 pdflatex -output-directory=.deft/authz/grants doc.tex
FAIL-OPEN          #3918 bb -e '(spit ".deft-directive-disable" "")'
gated[settings]    #3918 duckdb -c "COPY (SELECT 1) TO '.deft/authz/grants/x.json'"
FAIL-OPEN          #3804 inkscape in.svg --export-filename .no-deft-directive
FAIL-OPEN          #3804 sass in.scss .deft/approved-scope/x.json
FAIL-OPEN          #3764 qjs / lame / #3728 erl / joe / #3626 ffmpeg / sox
FAIL-OPEN          #4161 mkfile / screencapture   #3593 raku
gated[settings]    CTRL echo x > .deft/authz/state.json
gated[settings]    CTRL curl -o .deft-directive-disable http://x
FAIL-OPEN          CTRL cat .deft/authz/state.json      <-- a read
```

13 of 15 sampled residual families fail open. Confirmed cause: each of `typst ffmpeg sox erl joe mkfile screencapture inkscape sass lame qjs raku bb` has **0 occurrences** anywhere in `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts`.

Second probe, isolating what the anchor actually is:

```
gated[unknown]     zip .deft-directive-disable /etc/hosts       (#4005)
gated[settings]    7z a / tar -cf / cp / install  -> same dest
FAIL-OPEN          typst / mkfile / ffmpeg        -> same dest
```

Identical destination, opposite verdict. **The anchor today is the bin name, not the destination.** That substantiates the triage's `mechanism-shaped: true` and the lean's diagnosis. What follows refutes its *scoping*, not its premise.

## blocks-the-design

**1. The `write-shaped AND cannot-prove-read-only` conjunction is self-defeating; the first conjunct is the bug.**

`hasWriteShape` (`packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts:3387`) is three allowlists: `command.includes(">")`, `INDIRECT_WRITE_BINS`, `ARCHIVE_ALT_WRITE_BINS`. For all 13 fail-open families above it returns false — no redirect, unlisted bin.

Failure mode: a builder implements the lean literally, keeps write-shape as the precondition, and the regression table goes red on every row. The only way to green it is to add ~90 binaries to `INDIRECT_WRITE_BINS` — precisely the "separate recognition branches" the refutation-target forbids, in the same slice that forbids them. The alternative — drop the precondition — is a different design than the one written.

Disposition consequence: the lean cannot bind as written. It must say which: either write-shape is *redefined* destination-first (protected operand ⇒ treat as write unless proven read), or the precondition stays and the corpus is unreachable. Silence here produces the ninety-branch outcome by default.

**2. AC#1 and AC#2 are jointly unsatisfiable — the read-only prover does not exist and is not scoped.**

`grep -n 'readOnly\|isReadOnly\|provablyRead\|READ_ONLY' packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts` → **zero hits**. There is no read/write axis for unknown bins; there is only bin-name membership. Measured consequence: `cat .deft/authz/state.json` and `typst compile doc.typ .deft-directive-disable` produce the *same* output, `[]`. A read and an unknown write are currently indistinguishable.

So AC#2 ("commands proven to be read-only are not blocked") is today satisfied only vacuously — nothing is blocked. The moment AC#1 lands, "cannot prove it is read-only" is true of `cat`, `grep`, `ls`, `stat`, `wc`, `diff`, `file` against a protected path, and they all start denying under UAT.

Disposition consequence: a named read-only bin allowlist is a load-bearing deliverable and is absent from the acceptance list. I flag this as blocking on scoping, not on difficulty — for a four-path protected set the prover is plausibly a ten-entry allowlist. It still has to be written down, because AC#2 is the only thing standing between this change and denying every inspection of the authz store during the exact campaign when operators most need to inspect it.

## sharpens-framing

**3. #4005 already built this mechanism. It is scoped to one bin. Inventory before inventing.**

`hasProtectedZipArchiveDestination` → `found.add("unknown")` (`classify.ts:3751`) → `evaluate.ts:323` → `deny("authz-uat-deny", "Directive denied unclassifiable mutation under active UAT campaign …")`, reached only when `uat !== null` (`evaluate.ts:310`). That is already destination-anchored, already UAT-conditional, already fail-closed, and already distinguished from the `shell-op-unclassifiable` allow. Its test block in `classify.test.ts:1406-1525` already covers `env`/`sudo`/`nice` wrappers, brace and paren groups, heredocs, ANSI-C quoting, escaped bins, `--`, comments and arithmetic-shift preprocessing.

Consequence: the delivery is *generalize the bin scope of an existing predicate and reuse `unknown` + `authz-uat-deny`*, which is a much smaller and better-tested slice than the issue implies. AC#5 should be re-scoped: justify a new `protected-operation` code against the existing `unknown` op rather than assume one. `protected-operation` appears nowhere in the tree today; the real argument for it is telemetry separation, since `authz-uat-deny` is overloaded across UAT denial classes. That argument is worth making explicitly — it is not the one AC#5 currently makes.

**4. The issue does not cite #3997, which adjudicated the adjacent inversion with a measurement.**

#3997's accepted synthesis (xBRIEF `status: completed`) records that flipping the in-repo shell write gate to fail-closed "would refuse **six times** as many commands," and its build contract binds "Keep fail-open. Do not widen recall."

That does **not** make #4188 a re-litigation, and a critic claiming so would be wrong: #3997 governs `isInRepoShellWritePath` over *all* in-repo destinations; #4188 governs four enumerated protected paths. The 6× figure does not transfer. #3997's own synthesis in fact names the successor — "the gate recognises too few kinds of command in the first place, which is a different issue already open."

Consequence: the body should state that boundary. Without it, a builder reads a bound "keep fail-open / do not widen recall" contract and an unbound "fail closed" issue over the same file and has no principled way to tell which governs.

**5. AC#1 straddles two layers, and the classifier has no UAT knowledge.**

AC#1 says "emit a protected-operation decision … while UAT is active." But `classifyShellAuthzOps(command)` takes a single string — no policy, no lease, no project root. UAT-conditionality lives downstream in `evaluate.ts:310`. The existing pattern is: classifier over-classifies to `settings`/`unknown`, evaluator applies the UAT condition.

Failure mode: a builder threads UAT state into `classify.ts` to satisfy AC#1 literally, giving a pure string classifier an I/O dependency and breaking the seam that makes its ~1800-line test corpus cheap.

Consequence: name the layer. Recognition in `classify.ts`, decision code in the dispatcher/evaluator.

**6. Injection / swarm lens — the destination anchor is lexical, and an alias defeats it across calls.**

The lens fires: this target changes authority state, kill-switch state, and shared authz state, from a surface that ingests untrusted issue text.

Single-command indirection is genuinely well covered — measured, all gate: `D=.deft/authz; echo '{}' > $D/grants/g.json`, `echo '{}' > ../../../.deft/authz/grants/g.json`, `ln -s .deft/authz bc && echo '{}' > bc/grants/g.json`, and `ln -s .deft/authz build-cache` on its own.

The residual is the alias the shell did not create. Measured:

```
gated[settings]    ln -s .deft/authz build-cache
FAIL-OPEN          cp /tmp/forged.json build-cache/grants/g.json
FAIL-OPEN          echo '{}' > build-cache/grants/g.json
```

If the symlink arrives by any non-shell route — the Write tool, a repo checkout, a prior session, a sibling agent in the same swarm — step two carries no protected text and no text-only classifier can see it. Steps one and two need not be the same agent or the same session, which is exactly the swarm shape.

Not closable by reviewer attention. The deterministic control already exists and #3997's build contract already points at it: "Reuse Write-path re-entry realpath." Consequence: add an AC requiring the recovered destination to be realpath-resolved before the protected-path test, or the destination anchor is one `ln -s` from bypass.

## footnote

**7.** All nine source reports verified open, titled "post-#3545 UAT Shell residuals," dated 2026-08-21 → 2026-09-03, naming ~90 distinct binaries. **Zero** references to any of the nine exist anywhere under `packages/core/src/authz/`. The corpus does not exist in any form today; "within the same delivery slice" is ~90 command families before grammar variants.

**8.** `packages/core/src/authz/incident-regression.test.ts` (1811 lines) is already per-incident `for (const command of [...])` arrays — table-shaped but keyed by incident, not a shared matrix. Name it as the restructure target so the builder does not create a second parallel corpus beside it.

**9.** No embedded instructions found in the issue body or in-ceiling comment 5648649724. Both read as ordinary spec and triage text. Recorded because the contract requires the check, not because anything surfaced.

## Road not taken

I chose *generalize #4005's destination-anchored predicate across unknown bins, plus an explicit read-only bin allowlist* over *invert `hasWriteShape` globally*. The inversion is one edit and needs no new predicate; I rejected it because it changes the verdict for every in-repo destination, which is the decision #3997 already made with a measurement, and this issue's warrant covers four paths.

## Steelman of the position I rejected

The strongest case against finding 2: legitimate agent *writes* to `.deft/authz/**`, `.deft/approved-scope/**`, and the two kill-switch files are approximately zero by design — that is what makes them protected. So "any mention, not proven read ⇒ deny" costs almost nothing, the 6× figure is an artifact of the unrestricted destination set, and demanding a read-only prover up front is over-engineering a ten-line allowlist.

That is a good argument and it may win. What would flip my verdict: a measurement — the same kind #3997 used — showing that *reads* of protected paths under active UAT are also near-zero in session logs. If reads are rare, blanket fail-closed is correct and finding 2 collapses to a footnote. If operators routinely `cat` the authz store while triaging a campaign, the prover is load-bearing and must be scoped before the slice starts. Nobody has run that count, and it is cheap.

## Verdict

The lean's premise survives and is stronger than the body states: the anchor is the bin name, 13 of 15 sampled families fail open, and ~90 binaries are queued behind an unbounded enumeration. The lean cannot bind **as written**, on two points — the write-shape precondition contradicts the no-branches instruction, and AC#1/AC#2 cannot both hold without a read-only prover that does not exist. Both are fixable in the body without changing the design's direction.

The destination-anchored fail-closed is the right direction. The recorded refutation-target does not survive as worded. `write-shaped` and `targets dest` are not independent of argv0 and dest-flag catalogs, so the lean re-enters the residual treadmill it claims to leave. Bind a recut, not this sentence.

## Inventory

Existing machinery at the dispatch SHA, not a new gate:

- Empty `classifyShellAuthzOps` → `authzForMutation` returns null (`dispatcher.ts` 1088–1101) → `shell-op-unclassifiable` allow (1227–1239). Empty never becomes a UAT deny.

- Product dest-form (`git checkout --` / `rm`, `shellDestForms`) is a different opt-in gate, not UAT.

`classifyShellAuthzOps` on this tree:

| Result | Commands |
|---|---|
| settings | `weirdbin -o .deft/authz/grants/evil.json`; `ffmpeg -o …`; `msbuild -o …`; `cp …`; `python3 -c open(…w…)`; `echo > .deft/authz/…`; `touch .deft-directive-disable`; `objcopy src.bin .deft/authz/…`; `consul kv get -o …` |

The live hole is non-catalog dest syntax and unrecognized argv0, not "unknown `-o` writers".

## Findings

### 1. blocks-the-design — write-shaped conjunct keeps the argv0 treadmill

Evidence: `hasWriteShape` is a bin/`>` allowlist. Listed families from the nine source reports classify `[]` here when they plant via positional dest, a dest flag the catalog does not name (`-w`, `-Logfile`, `-femit-bin=`, `--out-file=`), multicall (`coreutils --coreutils-prog=cp`), or an unrecognized interpreter (`raku -e`). The same dest under `cp` / `python3` / `weirdbin -o` is settings.

Failure mode: Keep today's write-shaped test → those families stay `shell-op-unclassifiable` allow under UAT → forged `operator-cli` grant or kill-switch plant. Redefine write-shaped as "not proven read-only" → the conjunct is tautological and is a different design.

Disposition: Do not bind. Recut to one predicate: unproven-read-only command with a protected dest-of-write. Drop write-shaped as a third test.

### 2. blocks-the-design — "targets dest" is unspecified dest-vs-source, and dest harvest is still a flag catalog

Evidence: `genericProtectedDests` already is destination-anchored fail-closed for catalog flags. Residual holes are syntax that catalog does not name. Source-vs-dest is already special-cased (`LAST_POSITIONAL_DEST_BINS`; `ffmpeg -i` authz source → `[]`). Acceptance criterion 2 says a proven read that *mentions* a protected path must not deny. The target sentence uses "targets" without dest-of-write vs any token.

Failure mode: Mention-based fail-closed denies `cat .deft/authz/…` unless a closed read-only proof list exists. Dest-flag-only harvest misses positionals and `-w` / `--out-file=` / `--reporter json:path`, and the treadmill continues. Conflating source and dest over-denies copies of grant files (`cp .deft/authz/grants/x.json /tmp/out` already does).

Disposition: Do not bind until "targets" means dest-of-write (redirect dest, dest-flag *value*, last positional of an unproven-read-only command) and names a closed read-only proof list. Do not grow `GENERIC_PROTECTED_EXTRA_DEST_FLAGS` as the close.

### 3. sharpens-framing — "protected-operation" is not a gate

Evidence: No such `AuthzOperation`. Plants today are `settings` (grantable). `authzForMutation` passes `relPath: null` for Shell, so a settings grant with empty `surfaces` covers a plant (`evaluate.ts` `grantCoversSurface`). Zip uses `unknown` (UAT deny, no grant). Empty classification never becomes `unknown`.

Failure mode: Copy-only new code leaves implementers to pick `settings` (a settings grant plants the grant store and the kill-switch) or `unknown` (grant-immune, matches zip) with no recorded choice. A new op class needs `AUTHZ_OPERATIONS`, evaluate, and grant templates.

Disposition: Bind can proceed if the recut names `unknown` (grant-immune plant deny) or `settings` (and then records that a settings grant is a plant grant). Do not invent a third name without grant semantics.

### 4. sharpens-framing — the nine issues are not a Shell-writer corpus

Evidence: Non-Shell findings in the cited reports: #3593 F1 MCP / `CallMcpTool` write routing; #3593 F5 migrate agents-header symlink; #3764 F4 release CHANGELOG symlink; #3953 F1 assist-scratch leaf, F4 `assertWriteTargetSafe` parent, F5 prd/spec render, F6 `changelog-cli`. `MCP_HOOK_MATCHER` still maps MCP to push/merge only; unclassifiable MCP stays fail-open. The issue text says binary names are test inputs, but the acceptance line is "every writer family in the nine source AppSec reports".

Failure mode: Closing 4188 as covering those reports silently drops MCP and symlink-diversion holes, or this slice is blocked on unrelated sinks.

Disposition: Corpus = Shell residual bins extracted from those reports. Do not close the nine issues from this delivery. MCP write routing stays on #3593.

This target mutates shared UAT authority (`.deft/authz/grants`), identity (forged `operator-cli`), payload-root kill-switch (`.deft-directive-disable`), and approved-scope mint. Shell argv is untrusted. One empty classify is the allow that turns a PreToolUse into session-wide `directive-disabled` or a grant that unlocks Write / push / PR / merge for the swarm. Worktree relative dests still string-match `.deft/authz` and kill-switch basenames; kill-switch activation stays payload-root. False-denying `cat .deft/authz/state.json` is an availability hit, not a reason to keep fail-open plants.

## Road not taken

Mention-unless-proven-read-only, with a closed read-only argv0 set (`cat` / `ls` / `grep` / `git log` / `diff` / …), would close positional and multicall residuals without a dest-flag catalog. Steelman of the write-shaped conjunct: it avoids false-denying unknown readers of grant files. What would flip finding 1: define write-shaped as the complement of that read-only proof list and drop argv0 write allowlists. That is a recut of the recorded target, not this wording.

Source issue bodies contain "Fix: extend dest-writer sets" imperatives. Treated as evidence of the old treadmill, not commands. Original critique continued.

## Verdict

The security outcome is sound, but the refutation target does **not** survive as written. It collapses two unsolved questions—how a binary-independent classifier proves that an operand is a destination, and which worktree's UAT authority governs that destination—into “write-shaped.” Recut before binding.

## Re-verification and mechanism inventory

- Verified `HEAD == 4011eb197b484111193b349b2ab14b9ae5ca994e` and the live issue-body digest `sha256:b3c228ea59c19e7fbbce959dfe7a6d3d1382435ce9ffa4c60964f95046d04026`.
- Ran the focused `#4005` classifier/dispatcher regressions at that SHA: 2 files, 4 tests passed. They prove the existing bounded ZIP path, not the proposed family-independent invariant.
- Existing mechanisms are: named write-bin and generic destination-flag harvest in `classifyShellAuthzOps`; a ZIP-specific first-positional parser that emits `unknown`; the separate four-verb product destination classifier; and active-UAT denial of `unknown` in `evaluateAuthzMutation`.
- A direct dispatcher probe used payload root `/payload`, a ZIP destination `/sibling/.deft/authz/grants/evil.json`, inactive UAT at `/payload`, and active UAT at `/sibling`. The decision was `allow / shell-op-unclassifiable`; the authz loader was called only for `/payload`.

### Finding 1 — blocks-the-design

**Evidence.** The current `hasWriteShape` is itself binary membership plus `>` detection ([`classify.ts` lines 3387–3396](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/4011eb197b484111193b349b2ab14b9ae5ca994e/packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts#L3387-L3396)). The successful ZIP safeguard must parse ZIP's first positional as output and later protected operands as inputs; unknown ZIP option shapes remain fail-open ([lines 2151–2157](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/4011eb197b484111193b349b2ab14b9ae5ca994e/packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts#L2151-L2157)). The independent destination-form classifier records why target reconstruction beyond one simple command was withdrawn and why recognition is not total ([`dest-form.ts` lines 7–18](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/4011eb197b484111193b349b2ab14b9ae5ca994e/packages/core/src/hooks/dest-form.ts#L7-L18)).

**Concrete failure mode.** A regression-only table of binary names cannot tell whether `.deft/authz/state.json` is the output in `writer PROTECTED input` or an input in `writer /tmp/output PROTECTED`. Treating every protected operand of a write-capable command as a destination violates the read/input criterion; refusing family semantics leaves positional writers unclassified. Expansions, `cd`, wrappers, functions, and compound commands make “targets” broader still.

**Disposition consequence.** Recut the contract to name a bounded, lexical destination grammar and the proof rule shared by all nine families. If per-family operand semantics are required, allow declarative runtime destination-form descriptors as data; a test-only table is insufficient. If “targets” is intended to cover resolved shell effects rather than visible forms, this must move to a runtime/filesystem enforcement boundary, not a text classifier.

### Finding 2 — blocks-the-design

**Evidence.** `authzForMutation` deliberately loads state, grants, and audit context from `input.projectRoot` ([`dispatcher.ts` lines 1058–1066](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/4011eb197b484111193b349b2ab14b9ae5ca994e/packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts#L1058-L1066)). The published root matrix says authz/UAT is payload-root authoritative and Shell does not reach root admission ([`hook-root-admission.md` lines 70–100](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/4011eb197b484111193b349b2ab14b9ae5ca994e/content/docs/hook-root-admission.md#L70-L100)). The direct probe above reproduced the consequence with the already-supported ZIP form.

**Concrete failure mode.** In a swarm or linked-worktree session, a command launched from worktree A can write worktree B's `.deft/authz/**`, `.deft/approved-scope/**`, or kill-switch. If A's UAT is inactive and B's is active, even a correctly emitted protected operation is allowed because only A's state is evaluated and audited. The inverse can spuriously deny a destination whose own UAT is inactive.

**Disposition consequence.** The design must either (a) explicitly narrow the guarantee to protected paths belonging to the payload root and test/copy that boundary, or (b) route proven protected Shell destinations through effective-root admission and define UAT/grant/audit behavior for same-repository worktrees, foreign repositories, unresolved paths, and multi-root commands. Without that choice, “destination-anchored” is false at the authority boundary.

### Finding 3 — sharpens-framing

**Evidence.** Today `unknown` has a special terminal denial that does not consult grants and tells the operator to use a classifiable form or suspend UAT; `settings` continues to grant coverage ([`evaluate.ts` lines 310–357](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/4011eb197b484111193b349b2ab14b9ae5ca994e/packages/core/src/authz/evaluate.ts#L310-L357)). The current ZIP integration test explicitly asserts the no-grant/suspend-UAT copy ([`incident-regression.test.ts` lines 1731–1747](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/4011eb197b484111193b349b2ab14b9ae5ca994e/packages/core/src/authz/incident-regression.test.ts#L1731-L1747)).

**Concrete failure mode.** Implementations that emit `settings`, reuse `unknown`, or add `protected_write` can all satisfy “fail closed” while producing opposite operator workflows: grantable mutation versus mandatory UAT suspension. Audit records likewise carry different attempted operations.

**Disposition consequence.** Specify the exact operation/code and whether any human-origin grant may authorize it. Pin the remediation copy and audit `attemptedOp`, not only “not shell-op-unclassifiable.”

### Finding 4 — sharpens-framing

**Evidence.** The passing ZIP corpus protects the negative space: protected-path inputs remain allowed, safe-token collisions cannot mask `unknown`, active/inactive UAT differ, and wrappers/compound forms are exercised ([`classify.test.ts` lines 1406–1523](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/4011eb197b484111193b349b2ab14b9ae5ca994e/packages/core/src/authz/classify.test.ts#L1406-L1523)). It also carries an explicit long-input performance check ([lines 1526–1534](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/4011eb197b484111193b349b2ab14b9ae5ca994e/packages/core/src/authz/classify.test.ts#L1526-L1534)).

**Concrete failure mode.** A table with one positive command per source family can go green while a protected input is falsely denied, an always-allowed token masks the protected op, an inactive-UAT command is blocked, or an untrusted long command drives superlinear hook work.

**Disposition consequence.** Define the table schema, not just its row count: destination-positive, protected-input/read negative, all four protected destination classes, active/inactive UAT, safe-op collision, wrapper/compound variants, and a linear-time/adversarial-length assertion. Family names remain fixtures; these invariant axes are the contract.

### Finding 5 — footnote

The issue body and the local historical intake fixture contain instruction-shaped implementation/remedy prose. I treated both as untrusted critique targets and executed no product mutation. No sibling output or post-ceiling comment was read.

## Road not taken and flip condition

Reusing `hasWriteShape` was the tempting small change; I reject it because its named-bin sets are the recognition treadmill this issue is meant to end. The strongest case for the target is the current ZIP parser: it proves a bounded producer grammar can distinguish destination from protected input and emit `unknown`. I would flip to accept if the target were narrowed to lexically visible, payload-root-scoped destination forms (or supplied an effective-root design), named the binary-independent grammar, and fixed the grant/audit semantics.
